newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Trade Minister Kingsley Wickremaratne says government to set up regulatory body to ensure maximum benefits are derived from privatisation and trade liberalisation.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells labour unions to stop disruptive acts and campaigns instigated by corrupt union leaders. Government will have to expose corrupt activities of labour leaders if they continue acts detrimental to national interest.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga warns labour union leaders that sabotage will not be tolerated.
Buddhist monks to form national front to give people tired of party politics a new political philosophy and new ideas on national economic policy.
Buddhist monks demonstrate against plans to give lands owned by historic Digavapi temple.
Officials of Korea's Hanjung held hostage for four hours at Oruwala Steel Corporation by workers protesting against factory's privatisation.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga says power hungry politicians in plot to scare away foreign investors and sabotage country's economy. "This is no time to seek petty political advantage," she told public meeting in Biyagama.
